label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Renee,

First — I am sorry. I am genuinely sorry your toe hurts, and I'm sorry you're going through this. Nobody wants to read that their nail salon gave them an infection. If you read this and think I don't care, please don't. I do care about you, and I care about my niece.

I'll tell you what actually happened, as calm as I can.

On Oct. 24 you came in for a deluxe pedicure, $45. Your tech was my niece Vy. She's been licensed three years. She was born in Houston, so the "barely speaks English" part isn't true — she's quiet and shy, and I know that can come across one way, but you two talked the whole time and she understood you fine.

About the cuticle. During the pedicure you asked her to keep cutting, to go deeper, to get it clean. Vy told her not to cut too much, and you told her it was fine because that's how you always do it. I know saying that sounds like I'm putting all of it on you, and I don't mean it that way. She's my family and I love her more than anything. But I also can't sit here and let it be said she cut deep without the rest of it being in the story.

On cleanliness, because this is the part that hurt my family most. Every tool goes through the autoclave and comes to you in a sealed pouch we open in front of you. Your file and buffer were brand new, and she sent you home with them. The tub gets a fresh plastic liner for every person, every time. We passed our state inspection in August 2026 with no violations, and the certificate is hanging on the wall — you're welcome to come look at it. And if you've filed with the state, I'm glad they'll see the same thing we did.

When you came back to me on Nov. 2 and showed me the red toe, I did not shrug. I offered you your full $45 back, and I offered to pay your urgent care copay if you bring me the receipt. That offer is still open right now. What I turned down was $300 cash plus a year of free pedicures. That's a lot to ask, and I hope you can understand why I said no to that part. But the refund and the copay have never been pulled back. Bring the receipt, or call me, and I will take care of it. And if the toe isn't healing, please keep seeing the doctor and tell me what they say — I want this to go the other way and get better.

Now the hard part. Dave, you said it like every one of us is the same, like all these places are dirty. That one landed heavy. I've done this in Houston 19 years. I opened this salon in 2007, right after I finished working for my aunt. This has been my whole life. Until your post, I have never had an infection complaint — not one in all those years. When people say all nail salons are dirty, it takes something away from the ones that clean like crazy, and that includes us and the girls who work here. My niece read this thread last night and cried until she couldn't sleep, and she wants to quit. She's young and she loves this job. Please think about that when you write about us.

Renee, I'd rather talk than argue. You call the salon and ask for me by name, or you come by, and I'll stand there and talk with you until you're satisfied. My phone is at the salon and someone will always pick up.

Marisol — thank you. You said it just right. You said what you saw with your own eyes, that maybe it's worth talking to the owner again, and that you weren't saying Renee was lying. That took guts and kindness, and I appreciate it. Four years you've been coming to us, and I value that more than you know. If more people talked like that, half of these threads wouldn't even exist.

I just want your toe to get better. That's what I want.

— Lotus Garden Nails, Bellaire
